original.title: Perceived Usefulness, Perceived Ease of Use, and User Acceptance of Information Technology

core_idea: People's intention to use a technology depends mainly on two beliefs: perceived usefulness (it will help me do my work) and perceived ease of use (it won't take much effort). Intention then predicts actual use.
key_concepts_note: Use the concepts already stored for this theory in the library (theories.concepts).
when_to_use: Why do students, teachers, patients or employees adopt (or not) a digital tool?
Which perceptions predict intention to use a system?
Typical data: questionnaires with validated items, analysed with SEM.
common_mistakes: Adding many extra variables without a reason.
Measuring intention and claiming conclusions about actual use.
Using it to say why a system is useful; TAM measures perceptions, not design.
